data.content_ref: inline:{"analogy":null,"claim":"A large service with strictly more total internal redundancy is more resilient to correlated failure than a decentralized network because it can unilaterally enforce formally verified isolation domains, providing a mathematical guarantee of independence that decentralized operators cannot reliably coordinate.","counterconditions":[{"case":"The cost of formal verification scales super-linearly with the number of isolation domains, eventually exceeding the large service's budget and limiting the practical redundancy achieved.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"A zero-day vulnerability is discovered in the formal verification toolchain itself, invalidating the mathematical guarantees and creating a correlated failure across all 'verified' domains.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"Decentralized network operators successfully coordinate on a protocol that mandates and automatically verifies design diversity before allowing participation.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"}],"definitions":[],"derivation":[],"formalization_refs":[],"mechanism":"Strictly more internal redundancy within a single organization allows for the imposition of formally verified isolation boundaries. These mathematical guarantees ensure that failures in one domain cannot propagate to another. A decentralized network lacks a central authority to enforce such rigorous verification across all independent operators; relying instead on conventions that may be violated. Consequently, the large service achieves true independence, while the decentralized network only achieves apparent independence until a shared cause is found.","premises":[],"schema":"deepreason-reasoning-envelope-v1","scope":{"covers":[],"excludes":[]},"simulation_refs":[],"uncertainties":[]}
